rubric.why: Identifies chlorine’s electron arrangement or its seven valence electrons.
rubric.description: Chlorine has seven electrons in its outermost shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the shell arrangement 2,8,7 or for stating that chlorine has seven outer-shell electrons.

rubric.description: Chlorine accepts one electron to complete its octet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chlorine needs or gains one electron to attain a complete outer shell.

modelAnswer: A chlorine atom has the electronic configuration 2,8,7.
It needs to accept only one electron to complete its outermost shell (octet).

rubric.why: Recognises that gas particles are much farther apart than liquid particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that gas particles have large spaces between them or are far apart.

rubric.why: Connects the large separation of particles to lower mass per unit volume.
rubric.description: A gas therefore has less mass in a given volume and a lower density than a liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the particle spacing to lower mass per unit volume or lower density.

modelAnswer: Gas particles are much farther apart than particles in a liquid.
Therefore, a given volume of gas contains less mass, so its density is lower.

modelAnswer: At 100 °C, sulphur exists in the monoclinic form.

items.followUp: Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction of chlorine with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide.

rubric.why: Checks that the correct reactants and products are included.
rubric.description: Shows chlorine reacting with sodium hydroxide to form sodium chloride, sodium hypochlorite and water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct reactants and products.

rubric.why: Checks that the equation is balanced for the cold, dilute reaction.
rubric.description: Gives the balanced equation: 2NaOH + Cl₂ → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly balanced equation.

items.followUp: Write down any three differences between an element and a compound.

rubric.why: Distinguishes compounds from mixtures by how their substances are joined.
rubric.description: A compound is formed by chemical combination; a mixture is formed by physical mixing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this correct distinction.

rubric.why: Identifies the fixed composition of compounds compared with the variable composition of mixtures.
rubric.description: A compound has a fixed composition; a mixture can have variable proportions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this correct distinction.

rubric.why: Contrasts the properties of a compound with those of the substances in a mixture.
rubric.description: A compound has properties different from its constituent elements; components of a mixture retain their properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this correct distinction.

rubric.why: Distinguishes how compounds and mixtures can be separated.
rubric.description: A compound is separated into its elements by chemical methods; a mixture can be separated by physical methods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this correct distinction.

rubric.why: Contrasts the definite formula of a compound with the absence of a definite formula for a mixture.
rubric.description: A compound has a definite chemical formula; a mixture has no definite chemical formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this correct distinction.

modelAnswer: A compound is formed by chemical combination of elements; a mixture is formed by physically mixing substances.
A compound has a fixed composition by mass; the proportions of substances in a mixture can vary.
A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements; the components of a mixture retain their properties.
A compound can be separated into its elements by chemical methods; the components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods.
A compound has a definite chemical formula; a mixture has no definite chemical formula.

items.followUp: Write down any four properties of canal rays.

rubric.why: Identifies the straight-line propagation of cathode rays.
rubric.description: Cathode rays travel in straight lines.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cathode rays travel in straight lines.

rubric.why: Identifies cathode rays as streams of negatively charged particles.
rubric.description: Cathode rays carry a negative charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cathode rays are negatively charged or consist of electrons.

rubric.why: Identifies the direction of deflection of negatively charged cathode rays in an electric field.
rubric.description: Cathode rays are deflected towards the positive plate in an electric field.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are deflected towards the positive plate or by an electric field.

rubric.why: Identifies the fluorescent effect produced when cathode rays strike certain materials.
rubric.description: Cathode rays produce fluorescence when they strike certain substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cathode rays produce fluorescence or a fluorescent glow.

modelAnswer: Cathode rays travel in straight lines.
They are deflected towards the positive plate in an electric field.
They produce fluorescence when they strike certain substances.
